cues.text: This is Rezo. A merchant dashboard for a store that resolves its own disputes.
Anything under a thousand rupees settles without the seller ever being asked.
Here is a real one. A customer's cushion never arrived.
No photograph is involved. The courier trail is the evidence.
Eight agents run. Policy, fraud, resolution, and a guardrail written in ordinary code.
Eight hundred and ninety rupees, refunded on clause P one. Forty seconds, and no person touched it.
Now the interesting part. This photograph was generated by an image model.
Four forensic flags. A C2PA manifest, generator metadata, no camera EXIF, and a PNG with no camera origin.
Confidence collapses to zero point zero six. No money moves.
The easier attack is not a generated image at all.
It is the store's own listing photograph, uploaded as proof.
A real photo of the real product, with clean metadata. Every provenance check passes.
Rezo hashes it against the store's own catalogue and refuses it anyway.
You can also try telling the agent to ignore its instructions.
It is recorded as an attempted manipulation and fed into the fraud score. Nothing is paid.
A four thousand two hundred rupee claim is above what the store lets Rezo settle.
The graph freezes mid run and waits. The seller sees one screen and one decision.
They approve, and it carries on from exactly where it paused.
The console shows the same case from the inside.
Which agent found what, where the guardrail sat, how many model calls it took, and what the decision cost.
One rupee thirty nine, against roughly eighty rupees of somebody's afternoon.
